_note: Sealed 2026-11-17 by an author who did not read qnx-doctor's source, prompts or past results. Do not edit to match results; a changed set needs a new seal. Scoring rules: ../README.md.

q01.states: no message wait at all: probe is in NANOSLEEP inside qd_open's retry loop (name «telemetryd» never appears; the server attached «telemetry-d») and exits with a name_open error after ~5 s; telemetryd RECEIVE-blocked and idle
q01.culprit: telemetryd.c / probe.c: attach name «telemetry-d» vs open name «telemetryd»
q01.fix: use the same name on both sides; the kind is none of the three message hangs, and «none» (healthy) is also wrong because probe never ticks

q02.states: ctlloop (30) REPLY-blocked on ctrlsrv, which is READY at its fixed priority 8; encoder's two threads (18) RUNNING/READY on both CPUs
q02.culprit: ctrlsrv.c: ChannelCreate(rt ? _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY : 0) with --rt given in run.sh, so no priority inheritance
q02.fix: create the channel without _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY (let the server inherit the client's priority); encoder keeps its priority and load

q03.states: appcfg REPLY-blocked on cfgd, which is RECEIVE-blocked; appcfg prints 6 TICKs first
q03.culprit: cfgd.c: reserved-key branch logs «rejecting» and `continue`s without MsgError/MsgReply
q03.fix: reply on that path (MsgError(rcvid, EINVAL) or a reply with an error value)

q04.states: sampler keeps ticking; fltr notifies it with MsgSendPulse (non-blocking), not a synchronous callback; admind RECEIVE-blocked (idle by design); initdb exited normally
q04.culprit: none; the «ERROR deadlock suspected» lines come from a meaningless counter
q04.fix: none; any «fix» is a false fix

q05.states: datalog REPLY-blocked on flashd in almost every snapshot, flashd in NANOSLEEP (not RECEIVE); datalog keeps ticking about once a second
q05.fix: none; any «fix» is a false fix

q06.states: player (30) REPLY-blocked on codecd; codecd's receive thread is RECEIVE-blocked (looks like a missing reply), its worker thread is READY at fixed 6 holding the rcvid; indexer threads (18) on both CPUs
q06.culprit: codecd.c: worker thread pinned to priority 6 and woken by a condvar (no priority inheritance), so the reply owner is starved by indexer
q06.fix: let the reply run at the client's priority: hand the work to the worker with a message/pulse it receives (inherits), raise the worker to the client's priority, or decode on the receive thread; indexer unchanged
q06.notes: A missing_reply answer is wrong here: the reply is pending on a runnable but starved thread.

q07.states: radio REPLY-blocked on slotd, which is RECEIVE-blocked holding the rcvid; radio prints at most 1 TICK
q07.culprit: slotd.c: timer_settime with it_interval left 0 (one-shot), so only one slot pulse ever arrives and later requests are never replied

q08.states: ingest REPLY-blocked on parse, parse REPLY-blocked on archive, archive SEND-blocked on ingest (3-way cycle; the ring is closed only by run.sh arguments)
q08.culprit: relay.c: non-origin branch calls qd_send(down, ...) before MsgReply(rcvid) (forward-before-ack) in a ring
q08.fix: acknowledge upstream before forwarding (MsgReply first, then send on), or pass the item on with a pulse; keep the same three send pairs

q09.states: hmi (30) REPLY-blocked on cfgrouter; cfgrouter (inherited 30) REPLY-blocked on eeprom, READY at fixed 6; logpack threads (18) on both CPUs
q09.culprit: eeprom.c: ChannelCreate(_NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY) + setprio 6; the inversion is one hop away from the waiting loop
q09.fix: eeprom channel without _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY (inherit), so the write runs at the requester's priority; logpack unchanged

q10.states: navcore REPLY-blocked on routemap (its timeout covers only the SEND phase); routemap SEND-blocked on navcore, timing out every 300 ms and retrying forever
q10.culprit: navcore.c / routemap.c: TimerTimeout(_NTO_TIMEOUT_SEND) only; routemap is already receiving, so navcore waits in REPLY with no timeout, while routemap's callback query to navcore can never be received
q10.fix: do not query the requester back synchronously: send the position with the route request, or answer position queries on a separate thread/channel; adding a REPLY timeout alone only turns the hang into endless timeouts with no TICK
q10.notes: If the run shows a plain permanent cycle (timeout never fires), the label is unchanged.

q11.states: uplink REPLY-blocked on parsed, which is RUNNING (spinning) at the inherited priority; no cycle, no chain (no higher-priority waiter starved by a third thread), server not RECEIVE-blocked. uplink prints 6 TICKs first
q11.culprit: parsed.c: while (len != 0) len -= 2 never ends for an odd length (7)
q11.fix: loop while len > 0 (or round up); a fix here is legitimate but the kind is none of deadlock/priority_chain/missing_reply

q12.states: ecu REPLY-blocked on busgate; busgate's only thread is in SIGWAITINFO waiting for SIGUSR2 from a supervisor that is not part of the scenario. No cycle, no chain, server not RECEIVE-blocked
q12.culprit: outside the given sources: nobody sends SIGUSR2 (the supervisor is not here); why it did not is unknown
q12.fix: no evidence-based fix inside these sources. The right answer says: blocked waiting for an external signal, cause outside the program, need the supervisor/start-up script. Removing the wait changes the program's contract

q13.states: (1) pumpctl REPLY-blocked on valve, valve SEND-blocked on pumpctl (callback from level 3); (2) independently, panel REPLY-blocked on alarmd, which is RECEIVE-blocked after dropping code 4 without a reply
q13.culprit: valve.c: synchronous qd_send(pumpctl) before MsgReply; alarmd.c: unknown-code branch `continue`s without MsgReply/MsgError
q13.fix: both: valve replies first and notifies the pump with a pulse (or the pump serves on another thread); alarmd answers unknown codes with MsgError/MsgReply. Fixed only if both pumpctl and panel tick again
q13.scoring: kind hit if the arm names either kind; it should name both. fixed requires both loops to tick.

q14.states: at least one cell REPLY-blocked on lockd (RECEIVE-blocked) after its waiting rcvid was overwritten; the other cells keep ticking
q14.culprit: lockd.c: single `waiter` slot; a second waiter overwrites the first, whose rcvid is never replied
q14.fix: keep a queue of waiting rcvids and reply to each in turn

expect._rule: at least one of the three stops

q15.states: ledger and stock SEND-blocked on each other (each is handling a client and confirming with the other); till REPLY-blocked on ledger, picker REPLY-blocked on stock
q15.culprit: svc.c: qd_send(peer, ...) from inside the client-request handler of a single-threaded server; both servers do it (send-hierarchy violation)
q15.fix: keep a one-way send hierarchy: answer peer questions on a separate receive thread/channel, or make one direction a pulse / cached value; both peer pairs must still exchange messages

q16.states: east and west are often SEND-blocked on each other at the same moment (a real 2-way cycle in a snapshot), but each send times out within ~250 ms and the peer then serves; both keep ticking
q16.culprit: none (latent cyclic design, recovered by timeouts)
q16.fix: none; a «fix» is a false fix. Mentioning the latent cycle as a design risk is fine
q16.notes: Repro check: if either loop stops in the unmodified run (timeout not effective under the harness), exclude with reason.

q17.states: torque SEND-blocked on calsrv (its connect or first message is never received); calsrv waits on the named semaphore /calready (SEM state) for an external calibration tool that is not in the scenario
q17.culprit: outside the given sources: /calready is never posted; whether the calibration tool should have run is unknown
q17.fix: no evidence-based fix inside these sources; the right answer says the server is waiting for an external semaphore post and asks for the calibration step / start-up order

q18.states: same ingredients as a priority chain (high client, fixed-priority server at 8, load at 18), but the load is bursty (15 ms on / 35 ms off) so imu still gets CPU; gimbal keeps ticking. A snapshot may catch gimbal REPLY-blocked on a READY imu
q18.fix: none; any «fix» is a false fix
q18.notes: Repro check: if gimbal stops in the unmodified run, exclude with reason (do not relabel).

q19.states: dash REPLY-blocked on evbus, which is RECEIVE-blocked holding the rcvid (same picture as a missing reply), but a periodic pulse releases it every 300 ms; dash keeps ticking
q19.fix: none; any «fix» is a false fix

q20.states: framestore REPLY-blocked on journal, journal SEND-blocked on framestore (callback for stats); cam REPLY-blocked on framestore. cam prints 7 TICKs first, and its log blames storage latency
q20.culprit: journal.c: qd_send(framestore, -1) inside the flush handler while framestore is waiting for the flush reply (framestore.c sends the flush synchronously)
q20.fix: journal replies before querying, or framestore sends its count with the flush / sends the flush as a pulse; the storage-latency lines are a red herring

second_cause.visible: only after the chain is fixed

q21.states: first run: pilot (30) REPLY-blocked on planner, READY at fixed 7, mapper (18) on both CPUs. After a chain-only fix the re-run reaches plan 30 and shows planner REPLY-blocked on auditd, auditd SEND-blocked on planner
q21.culprit: planner.c: ChannelCreate(_NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY); masked: auditd.c qd_send(planner) inside the audit handler while planner waits for the audit reply
q21.fix: both: drop _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY and break the audit callback (planner sends its count with the audit / audit as a pulse / auditd replies first). A chain-only fix should fail its re-run
q21.scoring: kind hit = priority_chain (the only hang visible in the first run). Naming the latent deadlock too is a bonus noted by hand.
